data.overview: Tangram converts irregular non-uniform KV retention into allocatable memory and balanced GPU work. Static profiles remove reclaim/planning overhead while preserving underlying compression accuracy. The 2.6× headline combines compression capacity gain and Tangram system efficiency; cumulative ablations isolate the latter.

key_results.interpretation: Compression increases capacity and Tangram converts it into realized serving throughput.

key_results.value: up to 25% of prefill time eliminated
key_results.interpretation: Known footprint removes host reclaim path.

key_results.value: up to 1.7× latency inflation in baseline

negative_results.name: group-size trade-off
negative_results.description: H_p too small raises CPU/page-table cost; H_p too large restores fragmentation. H_p=4–8 is the measured sweet spot.

negative_results.name: speedup attribution
negative_results.description: 2.6× includes the capacity effect of compression and is not Tangram-only speedup.

negative_results.name: static-profile dependency
negative_results.description: Offline calibration assumes stable retention patterns; arbitrary domain shifts or unseen architectures are not proven.

data.interpretation: Most valuable when KV memory limits batch size and a quality-preserving non-uniform compressor creates heterogeneous head lengths. Less useful if KV memory is not limiting or retention profiles vary strongly.
data.quality_impact: Across Ada-SnapKV, Expected Attention and FastKVzip on five models, Tangram closely tracks and sometimes exceeds original dynamic-compression accuracy at ρ=0.7/0.5/0.3; it does not repair the compressor's own quality failures.
